paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of Fe-Al-Ti-B alloys with additions of Mo and W

evidence.quote: Four quinary Fe-Al-Mo-Ti-B and Fe-Al-W-Ti-B alloys based on Fe 3Al produced by vacuum induction melting were investigated regarding their microstructure and mechanical properties.
Four quinary Fe-Al-Mo-Ti-B and Fe-Al-W-Ti-B alloys based on Fe 3Al produced by vacuum induction melting were investigated regarding their microstructure and mechanical properties.

Four quinary alloys were prepared from high purity Fe (99.98 wt. %), Al (99.99 wt. %), Mo (99.99 wt. %), W (99.99 wt. %), B (99.99 wt. %) and Ti (99.99 wt. %) by vacuum induction melting under argon. A cold copper mould with Ø 18 mm was used for casting.
One part of each alloy was annealed at 1000 °C for 100 hours and cooled slowly under argon in the furnace.

The as-cast alloys show a Fe3Al matrix and a eutectic consisting of Fe3Al and a boride.
After 1000°C /100 h annealing the eutectics coarsened and the boride is distributed inhomogeneously along grain boundaries.

According to XRD the structure is face-centred cubic, space group Fm-3m with a lattice constant a0 = 1.035(1) nm. According to space group and lattice constant, the boride could belong to the large group of Cr23C6-type borides. However, the actual composition differs markedly from the theoretical.

At room temperature the compressive 0.2% yield stress of the Mo containing alloys is about the same as for binary Fe-26Al [27] while the yield stresses for the W containing alloys are about 100 MPa higher.

Stabilisation of D03 order combined with notable solid solution hardening increases the strength of the Fe-Al-based alloys [8].

At temperatures above the YSA the yield stresses of the investigated alloys are markedly higher than those of binary Fe-26Al [27] and are comparable to those of other Fe3Al-based alloys strengthened by boride precipitates [11].
Values for n of 3 - 5 are typically observed for Fe-Al alloys and suggest that creep is controlled by climb and glide of dislocations [38].
